title: School Operations Manager
description:
Job title: School Operations Manager

Location: The King Alfred School, TA9 3EE 

Contract type: Permanent 

Salary: up to £48,738 DOE. 

Salary: includes an element of recruitment and retention allowance

Working hours: 37 per week, all year round


The King Alfred School is looking for a dynamic Operations Manager to join our dedicated team. Reporting directly to the Headteacher, you will act as the vital link and enabler between our school and the Trust Central Team, ensuring our day-to-day operations are seamless, compliant and fully support our vision of a great education for every child.


About the role:

This role is designed to support our Headteacher, working alongside the School Leadership Team to streamline operations and maximise the capacity of school resources. This role will predominantly focus on facilities, compliance and management of the administration function as well as some HR and organisation of school events. This role is an embedded and respected role across the trust, valued by the school and the Senior Leadership Team but there is still an opportunity to make it your own. You will have an eye for detail in relation to systems and operational processes, and will be methodical in your approach to safety and compliance. 

The key aspects of this role are:

  • Building Relationships. It’s vital that you develop and maintain productive working relationships with the Headteacher, Leadership Team, Partnership Team leads and with the school staff. You’ll also be dealing with external contracts.
  • Communication. You’ll need to communicate effectively with all internal and external stakeholders in person, writing, electronically and by telephone. 
  • Compliance. You’ll ensure systems and processes are in place for effective management of essential reporting and contingency plans. You’ll be the first point of contact for facilities, recruitment, and the People team.
  • Operations. Coordination of critical school records will be your responsibility. You’ll act as liaison in relation to staff related safeguarding matters and data protection matters. You’ll manage the site estate team, take responsibility for the admin team and provide support to various school teams as required.


You will be joining us at a really exciting time with the arrival of our new Headteacher in September and the recent merger to form Pathway Trust. To ensure this role is perfectly aligned with our expanding trust and provides the best possible support to the school, the job description will be naturally reviewed and refined in the coming months as our new leadership and structures embed. 

The ideal candidate for this role will be:

  • Highly organised with the ability to manage their time effectively
  • A self starter who is capable of acting on their own initiative
  • Able to influence stakeholders at all levels and demonstrate strong relationship management skills
  • Confident in managing and implementing change
  • An exceptional communicator who is personable and able to build effective working relationships
  • A natural problem solver with the ability to spin many plates


About us

At The King Alfred School, we are proud to provide a first-class education in a safe, happy and caring environment where every child is supported to reach their full potential. Our Somerset location offers strong transport links, being only two minutes off junction 22 of the M5 and with a train station less than a mile away connected with all major rail links. 

We foster an ethos built on kindness, ambition, resilience and mutual respect, which is reflected in our broad and balanced curriculum and high standards of student conduct. We feature a thriving Sixth Form centre, a dedicated Community Council and student leadership team, the student-led Jill Dando News Centre and a strong track record of active involvement in our local community.

We can offer you: 

  • Happy, engaging students
  • A supportive trust and school community
  • Strong collaboration across the trust family of schools and access to a centralised team of specialists across all areas of school operations
  • A commitment to high‑quality CPD, with dedicated time and budget for your development
  • A values‑driven ethos where diversity, equity and inclusion are lived every day
  • Recognition of continuous service (modification order) to protect employment rights and entitlements
  • Local Government Pension Scheme with generous employer contributions and death‑in‑service cover
  • Access to a fully funded healthcare scheme for all employees and their dependants
  • Occupational sick pay to support you during illness or unexpected emergencies
  • Family‑friendly leave packages to help maintain a healthy work–life balance


In order to apply for this role please complete an application form by 9am, 2nd November. Please let us know if you require any adjustments as part of the process. 

Further details and additional information about our school may be viewed on our website. If you would like to have an informal chat about this role, please contact us to arrange that. 


Please know that depending on the number of applications received we may decide to close the advert early. If you do not hear from us by a week after the closing date then please assume that you have not been shortlisted for an interview. If you have previously applied for this role there is no requirement to apply again, all applications will be reviewed. We wish you all the best in your future and ask that you join our E-Teach Talent Pool so as to keep up to date with all of our latest current opportunities. 


Join us in Providing a Great Education for Every Child

Pathway Trust is committed to equal opportunities and encourages applicants from all backgrounds and communities, as we recognise the importance and benefit this has for our pupils.

This post is exempt from the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974. For further information on criminal record self-declaration for roles that are eligible for standard or enhanced DBS checks please refer to Nacro guidance and the MoJ website.

title: Senior / Staff Threat Intelligence Analyst, Hacks
description:
Headquarters: United States

 URL: https://www.trmlabs.com/

 About the Role

 When a protocol is drained, or an exchange is compromised, our customers need to know within minutes or hours which addresses to block and where the funds are going. You will own TRM's answer to that, end-to-end.

 As a Senior / Staff Threat Intelligence Analyst , you will lead TRM's hacks category: the metrics, the system that hits them, and the small contractor team that keeps it running around the clock. We align on the outcome; the approach is yours.

 The impact you will have

•
 Take command when a big hack breaks and act as a leader. Run the response: triage, coordination across teams, internal and customer communications, and the incident report afterwards.

•
 Get every major hack into TRM fast. Make sure every major hack is visible to customers within hours of the first credible public report, around the clock.

•
 Keep TRM's hack data complete and accurate. Every hack, at any size, is recorded with its entity, theft addresses, date, amount, and hack type.

•
 Follow the money at scale. Design the system, with our Data Science and engineering teams, that carries hack-specific attribution downstream as stolen funds move.

•
 Build the machine with AI. Leverage AI to build the tools and agents to automate key parts of hacks analysis and response, while ensuring human quality control over every output.

•
 Explain how it happened. Root-cause the most important hacks and publish best-in-industry technical analysis that makes TRM the first source cited.

•
 See the next one coming. Build approaches that spot vulnerable contracts before they are exploited, and get them into our product.

 What we're looking for

•
 5+ years of professional experience in blockchain intelligence, crypto investigations, cyber threat intelligence, incident response, or a closely related field.

•
 Has owned incident response in a high-stakes environment (exchange, security firm, incident response, or CTI team): war rooms, incident reports, communications under pressure.

•
 Strong blockchain tracing across major chains (BTC, EVM, TRON, Solana), including bridges, cross-chain swaps, and mixers.

•
 Understands how DeFi, bridge, and exchange exploits work, and how attackers behave after the theft.

•
 Applied AI fluency. We expect you to already be building AI-assisted or agentic workflows in your daily analytical work, to be able to show how you validate their outputs and where they fail, and to treat AI as a force multiplier.

•
 Experience managing contractors or leading a small team.

•
 Writes and briefs clearly, from technical deep-dives to executive summaries.

•
 Hands-on and highly accountable: does the hardest work, not only coordinates it.

 Nice to have

•
 Smart-contract reverse-engineering (Solidity).

•
 Experience at a security auditor or blockchain analytics firm.

•
 Experience following specific well-known hacker groups.

 About the Team

 The hacks function sits within TRM's Primary Intelligence organization, alongside the Facilitation & Money Laundering (F&ML) pod. You will work closely with the Nation States, Cyber Threat Intelligence, and Global Investigations teams, as well as with Data Science and Engineering on automation, and with Marketing on publications.

 Team Operating Rhythms

•
 Monthly metrics review with your manager.

•
 Weekly operating sync with your team.

•
 Regular syncs with your team across time zones.

•
 A war room, run by you, whenever a major hack breaks.

•
 On-call responsibilities

 Application Instructions

 If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.

 Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your skills and qualifications for the role.

 If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure your application will be considered.

 Interviewing with TRM

 Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while allowing you to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, an AI skills assessment, and a Leadership Principles interview.

•
 Recruiter Intro: Qualifications, motivations, and alignment with the role.

•
 Hiring Manager: Deep dive into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.

•
 First Round: 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role.

•
 Final Round: Hands-on case study. This is usually a panel-style session where we go deeper into your craft, problem-solving, and alignment with TRM.

•
 References: Former colleagues who can provide insight into your work and impact.

•

 Welcome to TRM: We're excited to build a safer world with you!

 Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way.

 AI Fluency at TRM

 AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM.

 We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.

 At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to:

•
 Accelerate repeatable workflows

•
 Structure and solve problems

•
 Improve output quality

•
 Increase speed and leverage

 You will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process.

 Life at TRM

 We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

 TRM moves FAST. We are a high-velocity, high-ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.

 Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.

 At TRM, you should expect:

•
 Priorities and targets to change quickly

•
 Operating with a high degree of ambiguity

•
 A high level of personal ownership and accountability

•
 Close collaboration across teams and functions

•
 Frequent, high-touch communication

•
 Creative problem-solving and out-of-the-box thinking

•
 A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes

 This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires thriving in ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.

 We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure-test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here.

 If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute.

 Leadership Principles

 We hire and grow against three leadership principles. They’re the standards for how we operate, treat each other, and make decisions.

•
 Impact-Oriented Trailblazer: We put customers first and move with speed, focus, and adaptability. We treat every plan like an experiment – test, ship, measure, and iterate quickly.

•
 Master Craftsperson: We care deeply about our craft. We balance speed with high standards, own outcomes end‑to‑end, and invest in getting better everyday.

•
 Inspiring Colleague: We add clarity and energy, not noise. We bring humility, candor, and a one‑team mindset — giving and receiving feedback to make the team stronger.

 Join our Mission

 At TRM, we care deeply about our craft. We are looking for individuals who want their work to matter, who experiment with speed and rigor, and who take pride in building a safer world for billions of people. If you’re excited by TRM’s mission but don’t check every box, we encourage you to apply — we hire for slope, judgment, and the will to learn fast.

 TRM is a Series C company with $220M in total funding, backed by Goldman Sachs, Bessemer, Y Combinator, Thoma Bravo, and others. Headquartered in San Francisco, TRM operates as a distributed-first company with hubs in Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York, Washington D.C., London, and Singapore.

title: Lead Counsel, Public Company Governance & Corporate Programs
description:
Headquarters: United States

 URL: https://www.hubspot.com/

 Lead Counsel, Public Company Governance & Corporate Programs

 Legal

 Remote - USA

 POS-20140

 The Legal Team

 HubSpot's Legal team is a proactive, business-enabling partner — not a back-office function. We help our teams move fast, smart, and responsibly, balancing innovation with rigor so HubSpot can scale as a publicly traded, AI-native company while maintaining trust, compliance, and clarity.

 Role Summary

 This is a role for a senior governance attorney who has earned the confidence of boards and committees, not just supported them. You will be HubSpot's primary governance lawyer — owning the company's governance policy framework, the NG&S Committee, the operational backbone for all three Board committees, proxy governance and annual meeting, and governance-focused investor engagement.

 The governance attorney who succeeds here doesn't just maintain recurring programs — they actively improve how those programs work, bringing the same rigor to process design as to legal advice.

 HubSpot is building an AI-first legal function, and we want someone who sees that as an opportunity to do governance work at a higher level of quality and scale, not as an obligation to satisfy.

 This is an individual contributor role reporting to the Director of Corporate Legal.

 What You'll Do

 1. Lead HubSpot's Governance Policy Framework

• Own HubSpot's governance policy framework, including committee charters, governance practices, director independence analysis, related-party frameworks, and Board refresh and skills matrix legal analysis.

• Lead the annual governance policy refresh, ensuring HubSpot's practices remain aligned with evolving NYSE requirements and governance best practices — and anticipating changes before they arrive.

 2. Own the Nominating, Governance & Sustainability Committee

• Serve as the substantive legal owner for the NG&S Committee, preparing materials, advising on agenda items, translating legal and governance requirements into practical recommendations, and supporting the committee chair.

• Advise on director independence, related-party considerations, Board refresh, and skills matrix analysis, with the judgment to resolve most questions independently.

 3. Run Board and Committee Operations

• Own the operational backbone for the Board and its Audit, Compensation, and NG&S Committees as a shared service across all three committees.

• Own the governance sections of HubSpot's annual proxy statement, including director biographies, skills matrix, committee descriptions, governance policy disclosures, and ESG and sustainability content, and lead the annual meeting process and logistics end-to-end.

 4. Lead Governance-Focused Investor Engagement

• Lead governance-focused investor engagement, including proxy advisor outreach related to Board composition and governance practices, and partner with Investor Relations on shareholder communications and proxy season strategy.

• Engage directly with ISS, Glass Lewis, and significant shareholders on governance matters with the preparation and credibility to represent HubSpot's positions authoritatively.

 5. Own Corporate Governance Programs

• Own recurring corporate governance programs (governance filings, D&O questionnaires, governance surveys, and related compliance obligations) with disciplined execution and strong records practice.

 6. Build an AI-First Governance Function

• You have a point of view on how AI and automation can raise the quality and efficiency of recurring governance work, and you act on it. You will identify and implement process improvements (including AI-enabled workflows) that reduce friction, strengthen governance operations, and increase the team's operating leverage.

• Build templates, playbooks, and governance infrastructure that make this function more scalable and resilient over time.

 What You'll Bring

 Required Qualifications

• 8-10+ years of corporate and securities law experience at top law firms and/or in-house, with at least 3-4 years of meaningful in-house experience advising a U.S. public company on corporate governance matters.

• Deep knowledge of public company governance (Board and committee practices, director independence, governance policies, stock exchange requirements, and related-party frameworks) with the judgment to own governance calls independently.

• Extensive experience supporting Boards and Board committees, with the credibility to advise on governance matters directly and translate legal requirements into practical, boardroom-ready recommendations.

• Meaningful ownership of, or a senior role in, annual proxy statement preparation and annual shareholder meeting processes.

• Demonstrated track record of governance-related investor and proxy advisor engagement; able to partner with Investor Relations and senior stakeholders as a peer, not a process manager.

• Track record of independently managing complex, recurring governance programs with strong attention to legal judgment, execution, and records discipline — and a drive to continuously improve how those programs run.

• JD from an accredited law school and active bar membership in at least one U.S. jurisdiction.

 Nice-to-Have Qualifications

• Experience working in-house at a publicly traded technology or SaaS company.

• Experience engaging directly with proxy advisors, including ISS and Glass Lewis, on governance matters.

• Experience advising on ESG or sustainability-related governance and public disclosures.

• Hands-on experience using or building AI-enabled workflows in legal or governance contexts, with a clear point of view on where AI adds real leverage in governance work.

 Where You'll Work

• Location: United States

• Work location preference eligibility: Remote

• Travel/Shift: No travel or shift requirements

 Application Requirements

• There is no application deadline for this role.

• Applications and resumes/CVs must be submitted in English.

• Cover letters are not required.

 Pay & Benefits

 The cash compensation below includes base salary, on-target commission for employees in eligible roles, and annual bonus targets under HubSpot’s bonus plan for eligible roles. In addition to cash compensation, some roles are eligible to participate in HubSpot’s equity plan to receive restricted stock units (RSUs). Some roles may also be eligible for overtime pay. Individual compensation packages are tailored to your skills, experience, qualifications, and other job-related reasons.

 This resource will help guide how we recommend thinking about the range you see. Learn more about HubSpot’s compensation philosophy .

 Benefits are also an important piece of your total compensation package. Explore the benefits and perks HubSpot offers to help employees grow better.

 At HubSpot, fair compensation practices aren’t just about checking off the box for legal compliance. It’s about living out our value of transparency with our employees, candidates, and community.

 Annual Cash Compensation Range:

 $165,600 — $265,000 USD

 At HubSpot, we value both flexibility and connection. Whether you’re a Remote employee or work from the Office, we want you to start your journey here by building strong connections with your team and peers. If you are joining our Engineering team, you will be required to attend a regional HubSpot office for in-person onboarding. If you join our broader Product team, you’ll also attend other in-person events, such as your Product Group Summit and other gatherings, to continue building on those connections.

 If you require an accommodation due to travel limitations or other reasons, please inform your recruiter during the hiring process. We are committed to supporting candidates who may need alternative arrangements

title: Legal Counsel
description:
About Us_
// At Masabi, we’re driving the fare payment revolution, powering the journeys of millions all over the world. We build fare collection platforms that allow riders to seamlessly buy and present tickets for public transport either on their mobile phones, from a ticket machine, or even by tapping their bank card to travel.

Our Justride platform is used in over 250 locations globally, including some of the largest cities in the world. With our industry-first mobile ticketing SDK, we’ve partnered with large players in the transport space, including Uber, Moovit and Transit.

Your own journey is important to us too. Choosing a role here means joining a network of innovators from all walks of life; a group of passionate individuals who consistently deliver. Here, you’ll find the tools you need to build the career you want. Whether you’re taking the direct route or trying a new path, we’ll support you no matter what.

The Role_

// At Masabi, we're building technology that makes public transport simpler, fairer and more accessible for millions of people. Behind every agency that runs on our platform is a commercial agreement someone had to shape, negotiate and close.

As our Legal Counsel, you'll work closely with our General Counsel, leading on our largest and most complex commercial deals.

Much of the work follows one opportunity from beginning to end. It starts with major tenders and public procurements, where you'll shape our position on the terms we can work with and the ones worth challenging. From there you'll take the deal through negotiation to signature, with colleagues across the business bringing the commercial and technical detail. Underneath runs the advisory side: data protection and privacy, IP and licensing, and the questions that come with operating across several markets.

You'll work directly with our CEO, CFO and CPO, helping them see risk clearly and decide quickly. Legal is a close-knit team, so you'll have genuine influence over how we work. Our biggest markets are the UK and North America, though we work well beyond both, so the jurisdictions and deal types will vary.

Location_

// This role is available on a remote basis for candidates located anywhere in the UK. Candidates based in London may also work in a hybrid model, with occasional travel to the office.

Responsibilities_

  • Take the lead on the legal side of major tenders and public procurements, shaping our position on the terms and where we're willing to move

  • Lead the negotiation and close of our largest customer contracts, working with colleagues across the business to settle the commercial, technical and operational detail alongside the legal

  • Carry major opportunities from first look through to a signed contract

  • Draft and negotiate across our full commercial range, including SaaS and licensing, implementation and professional services, NDAs, data processing terms, and partnership and reseller agreements

  • Advise the business on data protection and privacy, IP and licensing, and the commercial questions that come up day to day

  • Work directly with our CEO, CFO and CPO, translating legal risk into commercial choices they can act on

  • Use our AI and agentic tooling as part of how you work, and help shape where Legal takes it next

  • Step in for our General Counsel during periods of leave, or when he's committed elsewhere

About You_

  • You hold a law degree and a current practising certificate, qualified in the UK, the US, or a Commonwealth jurisdiction such as Australia, New Zealand, Ireland or Canada

  • Several years in practice since qualifying

  • You have strong, hands-on experience drafting and negotiating complex technology contracts, particularly SaaS, and have led those negotiations yourself

  • Communicates with precision, giving you a clear answer to a senior stakeholder without unnecessary detail

  • You're comfortable across a broad remit, moving between a major negotiation and a smaller advisory question in the same day

  • Has worked across more than one jurisdiction

  • You think ahead as well as answering what's in front of you, when the same issue keeps coming back, you'd rather change how it's handled than answer it a third time

  • Builds trust easily across a business, so people tend to bring you in early rather than once a decision is already made

  • You're interested in how AI can support legal work, with a clear sense of where judgement stays with you

  • Trusts your own judgement on risk, and you're comfortable standing by it

  • You can have the harder conversations with senior people and come out of them on good terms

We don't expect you to tick every box. What matters most is curiosity, a willingness to learn, and the motivation to take ownership of your work.

Nice To Have_

  • Public sector procurement experience, particularly in North America

  • Experience in public transport, mobility, fare collection, payments or another regulated infrastructure environment

  • Several years in private practice before moving in-house

AI at Masabi_

// AI is becoming part of how we work at Masabi. You don’t need professional experience using AI tools, but we’d expect you’ve experimented with them and are curious about how they can help you learn, solve problems, and work more effectively.

Some of Our Benefits_

  • 25 days of holiday per year plus the option to buy another 5 days, pro-rated

  • Private healthcare via AXA, including pre-existing conditions and mental health

  • Life insurance

  • Menopause support

  • Choice of workstation

  • The ability to work for up to 3 months per year from any country in the world (certain limitations apply)

  • Pension scheme

  • Training allowance of up to £1000 per year

  • £200 annual allowance for any home office need or improvement

  • Enhanced family leave pay

  • Cycle to work scheme

  • Regular social gatherings with a monthly allowance for each employee

  • A fun and collaborative environment with a focus on making a difference in the world

Careers at Masabi are for people going places - driven by a mission to make transit fair and accessible for all.

// We are a network of innovators from all walks of life, passionate about making a difference. At Masabi, we operate with openness and trust, creating an environment where everyone feels empowered to bring their whole, authentic selves to work.

Whoever you are, just be yourself.
// We welcome applications from underrepresented groups, including disabled and neurodivergent people, and can make adjustments at any stage of the process. You’re also welcome to share your pronouns whenever you feel comfortable. Together, we simplify journeys, remove barriers, and improve daily life for millions.

Why Join Masabi?

  • Driven by Purpose – We believe in journeys made simple. The work isn’t always easy, but the best things never are.

  • Encouraged to Accelerate – Masabi is going places and our people are in the driving seat. Whether you’re taking the direct route or exploring new paths, we support your journey.

  • Advancing with Empathy – We put people first and foster a culture of learning, not blame. No matter your cargo, we share the load.

We’re already powering journeys - are you ready to join us?

title: Manager, Customer Success
description:
About Ping Identity:

At Ping Identity, we believe in making digital experiences both secure and seamless for all users, without compromise. We call this digital freedom. And it's not just something we provide our customers. It's something that inspires our company. People don't come here to join a culture that's built on digital freedom. They come to cultivate it.

Our intelligent, cloud identity platform lets people shop, work, bank, and interact wherever and however they want. Without friction. Without fear.

While protecting digital identities is at the core of our technology, protecting individual identities is at the core of our culture. We champion every identity. One of our core values, Respect Individuality, reminds us to celebrate differences so you are empowered to bring your authentic self to work.

We're headquartered in Denver, Colorado and we have offices and employees around the globe. We serve the largest, most demanding enterprises worldwide, including more than half of the Fortune 100. At Ping Identity, we're changing the way people and businesses think about cybersecurity, digital experiences, and identity and access management.

The Manager of Customer Success leads a team of Customer Success professionals responsible for driving adoption, value realization, renewal, and expansion across a defined customer portfolio. This leader sets clear expectations, builds scalable processes, and partners cross‑functionally (Sales, Renewals, Support, Product, Professional Services) to deliver predictable customer outcomes and protect recurring revenue (ARR).

You will be accountable for the performance, development, and engagement of your team, ensuring they execute consistently against customer journeys, playbooks, and KPIs.

Key Responsibilities

1. Customer Outcomes & Revenue

  • Own renewal, churn, and expansion outcomes for the team’s book of business, in partnership with Sales and Renewals.
  • Ensure CSMs build and maintain strategic success plans for priority accounts, with clear business outcomes, owners, and timelines.
  • Oversee delivery of the annual department KPIs targets for the assigned regions under management.
  • Proactively identify at‑risk customers, ensure CSMs build and deliver save plans, and drive cross‑functional mitigation actions.
  • Use data (segmentation, health scores, product usage, NPS/CSAT, support signals) to prioritize focus and interventions across the portfolio.

2. Team Leadership & People Management

  • Recruit, onboard, and develop a high‑performing Customer Success team aligned to company values.
  • Set clear goals and expectations (KPIs, behaviours), and run a consistent rhythm of 1:1s, coaching, and performance reviews.
  • Build strong career development plans for each team member, including skills, certifications, and stretch assignments.
  • Model and reinforce a culture that is customer‑obsessed, data‑driven, collaborative, and accountable.
  • Address performance issues early with clear feedback, support, and structured improvement plans where needed.

3. Operational Excellence

  • Implement and continuously improve standard processes and playbooks for adoption, value realization and churn mitigation.
  • Drive effective use of Customer Success tooling (e.g., Gainsight/CS platform, CRM, support systems) for accurate data and workflows.
  • Own the team’s forecasting and reporting for renewals, risk, and expansion opportunities.
  • Ensure accurate and timely documentation in systems of record (success plans, notes, health updates, risk registers).

4. Cross‑Functional Collaboration

  • Act as the primary Customer Success point of contact for Sales, Renewals, Support, Product, and Services in your region or segment.
  • Ensure alignment with sales on program activities, account strategies, deal reviews, and exec engagement plans.
  • Collaborate with Marketing on customer engagement with events, advocacy, references, and customer stories from your team’s accounts.
  • Represent Customer Success in escalations and incident reviews, ensuring clear customer communication and follow‑through.

Required Experience & Skills

  • Customer Success, Account Management, Consulting, or related customer‑facing roles in B2B SaaS / enterprise software.
  • Experience leading and mentoring teams
  • Experience running a four quarter rolling churn forecast and delivering weekly exec level updates for an enterprise level book of business
  • Ability to be flexible and professionally manage change within your role and lead a team to deliver against business objectives within an evolving landscape
  • Strong organizational and prioritization skills with the ability to deliver under pressure and at pace while presenting a calm and structured approach to both direct reports and cross functional leaders
  • Proven ability to proactively own your book of business, taking the lead on interpreting data (health scores, usage, pipeline, churn trends) and convert insights into actions to deliver a successful strategy for your business that aligns to the wider corporate objectives
  • Ability to work and lead company programs cross‑functionally with Sales, Support, Product, and Professional Services.
  • Demonstrated experience driving customer adoption and value realization with complex, multi‑stakeholder accounts.
  • Comfortable working with executive stakeholders (Director, VP, C‑level) and leading structured, outcome‑driven meetings.
  • Excellent communication and storytelling skills (written, verbal, and presentation).
  • Strong understanding of subscription / ARR business models, renewals, and expansion mechanics.
  • Previous roles in Private Equity / VC owned businesses

Preferred Experience

  • Experience in Identity & Access Management (IAM), cuber security, or adjacent enterprise SaaS domain.
  • Hands‑on experience with Customer Success platforms (e.g., Gainsight, Totango, ChurnZero) and CRM tools (e.g., Salesforce).
  • Experience managing distributed / remote teams across regions.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

The Manager of Customer Success will be measured on a combination of:

  • Renewal Rate for team portfolio.
  • Churn ($ and %) against plan, with clear visibility of at‑risk ARR and mitigation status.
  • Expansion contributed or influenced by the team.
  • Coverage metrics: success plan coverage, EBR / Road Map / VU / SP review cadence, health score coverage and updates.
  • Customer advocacy: NPS/CSAT, references, case studies, and participation in advisory boards or events.
  • Team health and performance: retention, engagement, hiring quality, promotion readiness, and performance distribution.

Behaviours & Values

  • Customer‑obsessed: champions customer outcomes and long‑term partnerships.
  • Data‑driven: uses data to prioritize, decide, and course‑correct.
  • Team‑first leader: wins through collaboration, clear communication, and shared success.
  • Accountable: sets high standards, owns results, and addresses issues directly and constructively.
  • Growth mindset: embraces feedback, change, and continuous improvement for self and team.

Life at Ping:

We believe in and facilitate a flexible, collaborative work environment. We’re growing quickly, but remain true to the innovative, can-do startup values that got us here. Most importantly, we keep hiring talented, smart, fun, and genuinely nice people because that’s who we want to succeed with every day.

Here are just a few of the things that make Ping special:

  • A company culture that empowers you to do your best work.
  • Employee Resource Groups that create a sense of belonging for everyone.
  • Regular company and team bonding events.
  • Competitive benefits and perks.
  • Global volunteering and community initiatives

Our Benefits:

  • Generous PTO & Holiday Schedule
  • Parental Leave
  • Progressive Healthcare Options
  • Retirement Programs
  • Opportunity for Education Reimbursement
  • Commuter Offset (Specific locations)

Ping is the collective sum of all our individual experiences, backgrounds and influences and we pride ourselves in growing and learning together. We are committed to building an inclusive and diverse environment where everyone’s individuality is respected and everyone has an Identity. In recruiting for new colleagues, we welcome the unique contributions you can bring and encourage you to be your best self.

We are an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex including sexual orientation and gender identity, national origin, disability, protected Veteran Status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

title: Senior Product Quality Analyst - AI Voice
description:
The Personalization team makes deciding what to play next easier and more enjoyable for every listener. From Blend to Discover Weekly, we’re behind some of Spotify’s most-loved features. We built them by understanding the world of music and podcasts better than anyone else. Join us and you’ll keep millions of users listening by making great recommendations to each and every one of them.

We are the Voice Production Team, the creative team behind Spotify’s AI voice experiences. We think about AI voices from a casting perspective — including voice type, age and gender — and from a performance perspective, recognizing that a voice may need to perform differently for DJ than it does for an audiobook recap. We bring expertise in voice casting, direction, recording and production, and work closely with Speak to set the quality bar for AI voice models across experiences including AI DJ, Generative AI Ads, Personalized Podcasts, Agent Voice Chat and more.

As a Senior Product Quality Analyst, you’ll bring a dedicated evaluation perspective to the team. You’ll own how we define and measure AI voice quality, bringing together Voice Production’s creative bar, Speak’s technical bar and the wider industry bar. Your goal won’t simply be to determine whether Spotify has the “best” AI voice technology on the market. You’ll help us answer a more important question: is our technology the best at serving Spotify’s specific needs?

What You'll Do

  • Own the quality bar for Spotify’s AI voice models, defining what “good enough” means for different products, audiences, languages and use cases.
  • Independently design evaluation rubrics and build an evaluation approach that measures qualities such as naturalness, tone, pacing, pronunciation, accent, audio quality and overall experience.
  • Plan and carry out evaluation campaigns, turning qualitative and quantitative findings into clear recommendations for Voice Production, Speak and product teams.
  • Establish an ongoing evaluation rhythm, including when and how we reassess model quality as our technology and products evolve.
  • Benchmark Spotify’s AI voices against third-party models and competitors to understand where our experiences lead, where they differ and where there are opportunities to improve.
  • Help determine appropriate quality trade-offs as Spotify expands into additional languages and regions, considering the product use case and needs of each market.
  • Partner closely with voice experts, machine learning teams, product partners and vendors to maintain a consistent quality bar across demanding and sometimes competing priorities.
  • Surface the most meaningful gaps in model performance and use evaluation insights to help influence future research and technical priorities.

Who You Are

  • You have experience in product quality, evaluation, data curation or a closely related field where human judgment is used to assess model or product performance.
  • You know how to independently define evaluation criteria and turn subjective qualities into clear, repeatable rubrics.
  • You are comfortable designing and running both qualitative and MOS-style evaluations and synthesizing the results into actionable insights.
  • You have an understanding of voice or audio quality, including qualities such as naturalness, pacing, tone, accent and pronunciation, or the ability to develop that expertise quickly.
  • You have strong judgment and can maintain a consistent quality bar while balancing different product requirements, markets and stakeholder perspectives.
  • You are comfortable working autonomously, identifying what needs to be evaluated and establishing the processes and cadence to make that evaluation useful over time.
  • You communicate clearly across creative, technical and product teams and can act as a reliable point of contact for internal partners and external vendors.
  • You are curious about generative AI, speech technology and the evolving AI voice landscape and can translate changes in the industry into meaningful benchmarks for Spotify.

Where You'll Be

  • This role is based in London
  • We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

Compensation

Additional Information

Spotify is an equal opportunity employer. You are welcome at Spotify for who you are, no matter where you come from, what you look like, or what’s playing in your headphones. Our platform is for everyone, and so is our workplace. The more voices we have represented and amplified in our business, the more we will all thrive, contribute, and be forward-thinking! So bring us your personal experience, your perspectives, and your background. It’s in our differences that we will find the power to keep revolutionizing the way the world listens.

At Spotify, we are passionate about inclusivity and making sure our entire recruitment process is accessible to everyone. We have ways to request reasonable accommodations during the interview process and help assist in what you need. If you need accommodations at any stage of the application or interview process, please let us know - we’re here to support you in any way we can.

title: Senior Product Manager - Audiobooks Format Foundations
description:
We design Spotify’s consumer experience - end to end, moment to moment, across every screen, platform, and partner integration. Our mission is to make listening feel effortless, personal, and joyful for billions of users around the world. That means turning complexity into clarity across hundreds of touchpoints—from our mobile and desktop apps to the smart speakers, TVs, cars, and integrations where Spotify shows up every day. If it touches a consumer, we shape it. We bring deep insight into human behavior, design, and technology to craft experiences that feel intuitive, expressive, and unmistakably Spotify.

We’re seeking a Senior Product Manager to help lead the audiobook experience across Spotify’s mobile apps. You’ll join Format Foundations within Core Experience and partner closely with the Audiobooks business unit to shape how listeners discover, evaluate, enjoy, and build lasting relationships with audiobooks on Spotify.

What You'll Do

  • Lead product strategy for Spotify’s audiobook experience, shaping how the format becomes more engaging, valuable, and enjoyable for listeners, creators, and the business.
  • Define and evolve the experience across the audiobook journey, from discovery and evaluation through playback, library management, and reading.
  • Partner closely with the Audiobooks business unit to translate business strategy and listener needs into product innovation that supports growth.
  • Drive innovation across multimodal experiences, including the intersection of listening and reading.
  • Partner with Engineering, Design, Data, and other cross-functional teams to deliver intuitive, high-quality experiences at scale.
  • Use data, experimentation, and user insights to make informed product decisions and continuously improve the experience.
  • Build alignment across Core Experience, Audiobooks, Personalization, and other partners to create a cohesive Spotify experience.
  • Lead complex cross-functional initiatives end to end, setting direction and scope, creating alignment, and partnering with Engineering on delivery.

Who You Are

  • You have 5+ years of product management experience, including meaningful experience with audiobook, ebook, digital reading, or related consumer products.
  • You have a deep understanding of the audiobook or digital reading landscape, including user behavior, publisher ecosystems, and competitive dynamics.
  • You have experience building consumer products for mobile platforms such as iOS and Android, including complex user experiences.
  • You understand how to build scalable systems and experiences that help teams move faster.
  • You know how to balance user needs, technical considerations, and business impact when making product decisions.
  • You care deeply about creating intuitive, high-quality consumer experiences at scale.
  • You have partnered closely with Engineering, Design, Data, and other disciplines to bring products from strategy through delivery.

Where You'll Be

title: Solutions Architect
description:
About Vercel:

Vercel is the agentic infrastructure company, freeing people and agents to ship what's next. For more than a decade we've helped builders move from idea to production with speed, security, and exceptional developer experience.

Now we're scaling our products for both agents and people to ship and run software, built in the open and trusted by OpenAI, PayPal, Ramp, Supreme, and millions of developers worldwide.

About the role

As a Solution Architect in the Field Engineering team, you will span both technical pre‑sales and post‑sales, serving as a trusted advisor to our enterprise customers throughout their lifecycle. In pre‑sales, you will qualify technical fit, design future‑state architectures, run evaluations, and demonstrate how Vercel unlocks measurable business outcomes. Post-sales, you will act as a technical quarterback, helping customers successfully adopt and standardize on Vercel by aligning the right resources at the right time. You will guide architecture and implementation decisions, identify when to engage Professional Services or Developer Success, and work across Product and Engineering to unblock customers and drive long-term success for critical AI and Web workloads.

If you’re based within commuting distance of our London or Berlin office, the role includes in-office anchor days.

What you'll do

  • Partner with Sales to lead technical discovery, qualify customer use cases, and shape solution strategy for key opportunities.
  • Design target architectures for modern Agentic workflows, and AI and web applications on Vercel, including frontends, APIs, data and edge services, and integrations with headless and composable ecosystems (CMS, commerce, payments, media, analytics).
  • Create and deliver tailored demos, technical presentations, and workshops that clearly articulate Vercel’s value and differentiate our platform.
  • Own and run proofs of concept and pilots end‑to‑end: define success criteria, guide implementation, remove technical blockers, and ensure executive‑level outcomes are documented.
  • Act as lead architect post‑sale for strategic accounts, guiding onboarding, reference implementations, migration patterns, and best practices for building and operating on Vercel.
  • Proactively engage with customers on performance, reliability, and cost optimization, using metrics like Core Web Vitals, Lighthouse, and observability data to drive continuous improvement.
  • Collaborate with other members of the Field Engineering Team to standardise playbooks, reusable assets, and patterns that scale across customers and regions.
  • Respond to and coordinate security, compliance, and architecture reviews, partnering with internal specialists on areas like data protection and regulatory requirements.
  • Capture recurring themes, patterns, and gaps from the field and feed them back into Product and Engineering roadmaps as the technical Voice of the Customer.
  • Contribute to internal enablement and external content (reference architectures, example repos, talks, and blog posts) that help developers be successful on Vercel.
  • Some travel elements are expected relating to industry events, customer on-sites.

What you need

  • You have significant experience in a customer‑facing technical role (solutions architect, sales engineer, platform architect, Agency Software Engineer) working with modern web or cloud platforms.
  • You bring strong hands‑on skills with JavaScript/TypeScript and modern web frameworks, ideally including Next.js, and are comfortable reviewing and discussing application code with engineering teams.
  • You understand web performance, caching, networking, and security fundamentals, ideally AI/LLM powered applications and Agentic workflows and can translate them into practical guidance for enterprise architectures.
  • You are equally comfortable discussing business outcomes with executives and implementation details with developers, switching context quickly while maintaining credibility.
  • You have a track record of owning complex technical projects, juggling multiple stakeholders, and delivering on time in fast‑moving environments.
  • You thrive in collaborative field teams, enjoy mentoring others, and value clear, concise communication and documentation.
  • You are familiar with cloud platforms (such as AWS, Azure, or GCP) and how SaaS and edge platforms integrate into broader enterprise architectures.
  • You have empathy for developers and a passion for great developer experience, and you enjoy helping teams build accurate mental models of how platforms work.
  • Bonus if you have experience of building AI powered applications, or Agentic workloads, ideally leveraging tooling such as the AI SDK.

Bonus if you

  • Have production experience deploying and operating Next.js or other modern frontend frameworks on Vercel or similar platforms.
  • Have worked with organisations standardising on composable architectures (headless CMS, commerce, search, analytics, and identity providers).
  • Hold cloud or architecture certifications (for example, Cloud Solutions Architect certifications) or have led large‑scale migrations to cloud‑native platforms.
  • Are familiar with security and privacy standards such as SOC 2, PCI DSS, or HIPAA and have participated in customer security reviews.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation package, including equity.
  • Inclusive Healthcare Package.
  • Learn and Grow - we provide mentorship and send you to events that help you build your network and skills.
  • Flexible Time Off.
  • We will provide you the gear you need to do your role, and a WFH budget for you to outfit your space as needed.

description:
Headquarters: Remote - California

 Our mission at Duolingo is to develop the best education in the world and make it universally available. It’s a big mission, and that’s where you come in!

 At Duolingo, you’ll join a team that cares about educating our users, experimenting with big ideas, making fact-based decisions, and finding innovative solutions to complex problems. You’ll have limitless learning opportunities and daily collaborations with world-class minds — while doing work that’s both meaningful and fun.

 Join our life-changing mission to develop education for our half a billion (and growing!) learners around the world.

 Read our blog to learn more.

 About the role...

 Join us to build Duolingo Ads, Duolingo’s direct ad business. Most learners use our free, ad‑supported app—so great ads are core to our mission. We’re hiring a Head of West Coast Sales to open and scale our West Coast region. You will set regional strategy, build and lead a high‑performing team, and own revenue outcomes across priority verticals and agency holding companies. As a player/coach, you’ll cultivate senior‑level relationships, shape pricing and packaging with leadership, and close high‑impact deals that both delight learners and drive revenue while leading a team of sellers. This is a high‑ownership, early‑stage opportunity to help define how ads show up for hundreds of millions of learners while building a repeatable, data‑driven go‑to‑market.

title: Chief of Staff, CCO
description:
Headquarters: USA - Remote

 About Ping Identity:

 At Ping Identity, we believe in making digital experiences both secure and seamless for all users, without compromise. We call this digital freedom. And it's not just something we provide our customers. It's something that inspires our company. People don't come here to join a culture that's built on digital freedom. They come to cultivate it.

 Our intelligent, cloud identity platform lets people shop, work, bank, and interact wherever and however they want. Without friction. Without fear.

 While protecting digital identities is at the core of our technology, protecting individual identities is at the core of our culture. We champion every identity. One of our core values, Respect Individuality, reminds us to celebrate differences so you are empowered to bring your authentic self to work.

 We're headquartered in Denver, Colorado and we have offices and employees around the globe. We serve the largest, most demanding enterprises worldwide, including more than half of the Fortune 100. At Ping Identity, we're changing the way people and businesses think about cybersecurity, digital experiences, and identity and access management.

 We are seeking a strategic and analytical Chief of Staff to partner with our Chief Customer Officer (CCO) in driving business performance across our Customer organization. This role combines financial and operational strategy, data-driven decision-making, and cross-functional collaboration to improve customer retention, revenue performance, and organizational effectiveness.

 The ideal candidate brings strong financial and business acumen, a collaborative mindset, and the ability to translate complex information into actionable insights that inform executive decisions and strengthen financial and operational accountability.

 What You'll Do

• Customer revenue metrics: In partnership with Finance, which owns ARR and financial reporting, to ensure customer metrics (ARR movement, gross and net revenue retention, renewal rates on up for renewal revenue, cohort views and churn drivers) follow Thoma Bravo standards and best-in-class methods. Translates those metrics into the customer organization's view, measures renewal forecast accuracy, and reports on cross-sell and upsell pipeline, which Renewals and Sales own.

• Executive and board narrative: Prepares the CCO's materials for the executive leadership team, board, Thoma Bravo operating reviews and QBRs, framing performance, risk and investment asks in terms of business outcomes. Ensures what the board sees reconciles to how the organization operates.

• Renewal and retention reporting: Owns renewal rate reporting and variance analysis of the official forecast against plan and actuals, explaining the drivers behind the numbers.

• Renewal and retention plan and resource models: In partnership with Finance, builds the customer organization's annual renewal and retention plan (historical baselines, renewal rate assumptions and targets) and the headcount, coverage-ratio and capacity models tied to book-of-business segmentation.

• Customer health and signals: Delivers the customer health scoring model and churn and risk analysis.

• Customer reporting requirements and CCO analysis: Sets the customer organization's reporting requirements across Salesforce, the data warehouse and BI tools, aligned with Finance's metric definitions, which Systems & Operations and Data & Analytics build to. Handles the CCO's own analysis and reporting requests.

• Cross-functional Alignment: Works with Revenue Operations and CRO leadership team to align on strategies and reporting for improving Net Retention Rate. Works with the Product Strategy team to align on churn analysis and forecasting by product.

 What You'll Bring

• Significant experience in strategic finance, FP&A, business operations, revenue operations, customer success operations, or a related field, ideally within a B2B SaaS environment.

• Strong understanding of SaaS business models and recurring revenue metrics, including ARR, GRR, NRR, renewals, and churn.

• Experience translating business needs into reporting and analytics requirements, with familiarity using tools such as Salesforce, Excel, SQL, Power BI, or Tableau.

• Ability to analyze complex datasets and communicate insights clearly to executive audiences.

• Familiarity with CRM, reporting, and business intelligence tools such as Salesforce, Excel, SQL, Power BI, or Tableau.

• Strong collaboration, communication, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to influence across teams.

• Experience in private equity-backed environments or supporting executive and board-level reporting is a plus.

 Salary Range: $155,628 - $207,504

 In accordance with Colorado’s Equal Pay for Equal Work Act (SB 19-085) the approximate compensation range for this role in Colorado is listed above. Final compensation for this role will be determined by various factors, such as knowledge, skills, and abilities.
 Life at Ping:

 We believe in and facilitate a flexible, collaborative work environment. We’re growing quickly, but remain true to the innovative, can-do startup values that got us here. Most importantly, we keep hiring talented, smart, fun, and genuinely nice people because that’s who we want to succeed with every day.

 Here are just a few of the things that make Ping special:

• A company culture that empowers you to do your best work.

• Employee Resource Groups that create a sense of belonging for everyone.

• Regular company and team bonding events.

• Competitive benefits and perks.

• Global volunteering and community initiatives

 Our Benefits:

• Generous PTO & Holiday Schedule

• Parental Leave

• Progressive Healthcare Options

• Retirement Programs

• Opportunity for Education Reimbursement

• Commuter Offset (Specific locations)

 Ping is the collective sum of all our individual experiences, backgrounds and influences and we pride ourselves in growing and learning together. We are committed to building an inclusive and diverse environment where everyone’s individuality is respected and everyone has an Identity. In recruiting for new colleagues, we welcome the unique contributions you can bring and encourage you to be your best self.

 We are an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex including sexual orientation and gender identity, national origin, disability, protected Veteran Status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

title: Customer Enablement Manager
description:
Headquarters: Remote

 As a Customer Enablement Manager, you will partner with complex enterprise customers to transform how work gets done across their organizations. You will own a portfolio of strategic customers, providing a variety of enablement activities, including discovery, workflow consultation, change management, strategic enablement, and scalable education to accelerate adoption and measurable business outcomes.

 You will work closely with Customer Success, Sales, and Services to understand customer priorities, diagnose barriers to adoption, and recommend strategies that help organizations adopt new workflows and AI-enabled ways of working. As a senior individual contributor, you will serve as a trusted advisor to customers and internal partners, navigate complex stakeholder environments, and help shape repeatable approaches that strengthen Asana's broader Customer Enablement practice.

 This role is West Coast based remote and is open to employees in Pacific or Mountain Standard time.

 What you'll achieve

• Strategic Trusted Advisory: Develop a deep understanding of customer business priorities, operating models, and ways of working. Lead discovery with complex stakeholders and translate customer challenges into clear recommendations for workflow, enablement, and adoption strategies that drive measurable business value.

• Own Complex Customer Engagements: Independently manage complex enterprise engagements within your portfolio of strategic customers, from discovery and planning through delivery, measurement, and follow-through. Navigate ambiguity, competing priorities, and multi-stakeholder environments while keeping engagements aligned to customer and account outcomes.

• Drive Workflow and AI Transformation: Help customers rethink how work gets done by translating Asana and AI capabilities into practical, scalable use cases. Guide customers through the people, process, and behavior change required to successfully adopt new ways of working.

• Executive and High-Impact Facilitation: Design and facilitate workflow consultations, strategic workshops, enablement programs, and executive-level conversations for audiences ranging from end users and champions to senior leaders. Adapt your approach based on customer maturity, organizational complexity, and desired outcomes.

• Measure and Optimize Customer Impact: Use adoption, engagement, and efficacy data to assess whether enablement is driving meaningful behavior change and business outcomes. Identify trends, adjust engagement strategies, and use insights to strengthen customer plans and CEM programs.

• Strengthen Customer Partnerships and Commercial Outcomes: Identify risks, expansion opportunities, and new use cases through your customer engagements. Partner with account teams to connect adoption and enablement strategies to retention, expansion, and long-term customer value.

 About you

• 6+ years of experience in customer enablement, customer success, strategic consulting, implementation, change management, professional services, or a related customer-facing role, ideally within SaaS.

• Demonstrated experience independently leading complex enterprise customer engagements that combine discovery, consultation, facilitation, and enablement to drive adoption, behavior change, or business transformation.

• Strong consultative skills with the ability to uncover root causes, synthesize complex information, challenge assumptions constructively, and translate ambiguity into clear recommendations and action plans.

• Experience engaging and influencing senior and executive stakeholders, including navigating competing priorities and building alignment across diverse stakeholder groups.

• Excellent facilitation and communication skills, with the ability to lead strategic conversations and high-impact sessions for audiences ranging from practitioners to executives.

• Strong project and portfolio management skills, with a track record of independently managing multiple complex customer engagements and driving work forward without significant oversight.

The Experience

You're Our Person If...

Even Better If...

  • You have security or technology marketing experience, including CISO or Gartner executive programs.
  • You have experience with CRM, campaign management and marketing reporting tools.
  • You have mentored junior colleagues.

Unleash Your Potential

When you join Salesforce, you'll be limitless in all areas of your life. Our benefits and resources support you to find balance and be your best, and our AI agents accelerate your impact so you can do your best. Together, we'll bring the power of Agentforce to organizations of all sizes and deliver amazing experiences that customers love. Apply today to not only shape the future - but to redefine what's possible - for yourself, for AI, and the world.

description:
Speech and Language Therapist

Location: Central role assigned to academies in Manchester, Stoke & the Wirral

Salary: NJC SCP 40-46

Contract Type: Permanent, full-time or 0.8FTE. Term-time only plus 10 days

Make a Real Difference Where It Matters Most

Are you a passionate Speech and Language Therapist looking to transform outcomes for children and young people with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND)?

At Co-op Academies Trust, we are looking for dedicated, forward-thinking Speech and Language Therapists to join our collaborative regional networks. Many of our schools serve areas facing high levels of deprivation across the North of England. In this unique role, you won’t just manage a caseload; you will work alongside school staff, SENCOs, and external partners to build long-term capacity, upskill teaching teams, and create truly communication-friendly environments.

Key Responsibilities

  1. Deliver individual and group speech, language, and communication assessments and evidence-based interventions for pupils with complex needs, including Autism Spectrum Condition (ASC), ADHD, and sensory processing needs.
  2. Work closely with school SENCOs, teachers, and support staff to embed practical speech and language strategies across the wider curriculum.
  3. Design and deliver high-quality training and practical workshops for school staff, parents, and carers.
  4. Collaborate alongside existing NHS Speech and Language Therapy provisions to maximise support capacity across our primary and secondary academies.
  5. Contribute to Education, Health, and Care Plans (EHCPs), maintaining thorough records in accordance with HCPC and RCSLT standards.

What We Are Looking For

  1. Qualifications: Recognised Degree in Speech and Language Therapy and active registration with the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC).
  2. Experience: Proven experience working in inclusive educational settings with young people with SEND and complex learning or communication needs.
  3. Skills: Strong collaborative skills, expertise in Alternative and Augmentative Communication (AAC), ability to produce high-quality clinical reports, and a passion for empowering school staff.
  4. Values: A clear commitment to co-operative principles, inclusion, equal opportunities, and public service.

Why Choose Co-op Academies Trust?

  1. Values-Driven Culture: Guided by our Ways of Being Co-op (Do what matters most, Be yourself always, Show you care, Succeed together), we place ethics, equity, and community at the heart of everything we do.
  2. Dedicated Supervision & Professional Growth: Access clinical supervision, peer support networks, and ongoing continuous professional development (CPD).
  3. Competitive Employee Benefits: Local Government Pension Scheme, Co-op staff discounts, and access to a wide range of health and wellbeing benefits.

How to Apply

Ready to join an organisation dedicated to improving children's life chances? Please follow the online application process to be considered. For an informal conversation about the role, please contact Natalie Jones (natalie.jones@coopacademies.co.uk)

As a supporter, advocate and coach for your caseload of learners, you will be ideally placed to drive success so that young people are able to realise their ambitions.

The successful candidate will be responsive, adaptive and flexible and will embrace challenge, to break down barriers and drive improvement and development, both academic and pastorally.

What You Will Do

  • Support learners with High Needs and Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) to thrive and make progress throughout their educational experience at Leeds City College.
  • Working in classes on a one-to-one or small group basis, you will make sure learners engage with theory, practical and English and Mathematics lessons so that they can succeed. You’ll also work outside the classroom when required, creating an informal yet productive environment which allow learners to learn at their own pace.
  • Work closely with curriculum and support colleagues, teaching, assessing and giving feedback to learners, encouraging them to improve and achieve consistently. This might include devising appropriate learning resources, alternative assessment methods, working with other internal and external colleagues to scaffold and bolster learners.
  • Your approach will be professional, approachable and flexible so that best possible outcomes for learners are realised.
  • You will take responsibility for record keeping, with a keen eye for a detail and accuracy and an understanding of the importance of maintaining a full account of a learner’s journey.
  • You will base your practice on a Restorative Practice approach, amicably resolving difficult circumstances when they arise, so that learners remain engaged and focused.

About You

  • You will be a motivated and committed person who is keen to see others develop and grow their skills, abilities and experience.
  • With learners at the heart of your practice, you will be professional and enthusiastic, with the ability to think quickly, using a range of strategies to maintain learner focus and engagement, regularly reviewing and updating a range of documents to record, monitor and review progress.
  • With a patient approach, a “can do” attitude, a strong team working ethic and the ability to provide structure and guidelines to learners, you will be at the forefront of their development.

title: Mathematics Mentor
description:
The Kingston Academy seeks an ambitious and motivated Mathematics Mentor to offer additional support to pupils by developing, creating and implementing a range of interventions and coaching strategies.

The Kingston Academy is a high-performing, inclusive secondary school founded in 2015. Today we educate over 1,400 pupils from Year 7 through to Sixth Form and are proud to serve our diverse and vibrant community.
In 2025, we were recognised as one of the Top 10 best non-selective state schools in the UK based on GCSE outcomes, reflecting our strong culture of aspiration, exceptional teaching, and commitment to every child’s success. The school was also named among the Top 50 happiest schools in the UK in Ofsted’s official wellbeing survey — a testament to the positive relationships, high standards of behaviour and supportive environment that underpin our ethos.
We are proudly inclusive, with a specialist resource provision (SRP) for pupils whose primary need is Autism Spectrum Condition, ensuring that all young people are able to learn, thrive and belong.

Our Mathematics Mentor will play a key role in strengthening pupils’ mathematical foundations, confidence and fluency, with a particular focus on targeted numeracy interventions in the younger year groups.

Working closely with the Mathematics Department and wider teaching teams, the successful candidate will help identify and address gaps in learning through structured interventions, in-class support and individual or small-group teaching. They will build positive relationships with pupils, helping them overcome barriers and make strong progress in mathematics.

This role is particularly suited to a graduate or suitably qualified individual considering a career in Mathematics teaching. Working alongside experienced teachers, the successful candidate will gain valuable classroom experience, develop their teaching skills and take meaningful steps towards entering the profession, while making a real difference to pupils’ confidence and achievement.

Our commitment extends not only to pupils but also to the people who work with them every day. We are dedicated to attracting, retaining and sustaining an expert workforce through high-quality talent development, ensuring that our staff are skilled, motivated and well supported. By investing in professional learning, coaching, wellbeing and leadership pathways, we ensure that our staff can flourish — and that our students benefit from consistently excellent teaching.

We invite applications from candidates with the following attributes for this role:

  • Have strong mathematical knowledge and the ability to explain mathematical concepts clearly and accurately.

  • Be able to communicate effectively with pupils of different ages and abilities.

  • Ambition to develop each child to their maximum potential.

  • Flexible and approachable, resilient and calm under pressure, and demonstrate good judgement.

Benefits of working at The Kingston Academy:

  • Generous pay-scales, regularly paying 1% higher than National Support Staff Pay Scales;

  • 2-week October Half Term break;

  • Access to subsidised Cycle to Work scheme;

  • Weekly Professional Development sessions at whole-school and departmental level;

  • Generous pension scheme;

  • Subsidised study at Kingston University at Masters and Doctorate Level;

  • Flexible working arrangements may be considered on request;

  • Access to Employee Assistance Programme, subsidised eye test and flu vaccinations;

  • Work in a vibrant, supportive school environment where staff wellbeing is prioritised.

More details are available on the Candidate Information Pack, Job Description and Person Specification.

Interview Procedure

Our selection procedure will aim to identify with rigour whether the candidate fulfils the requirements of the post and will include the consideration of the candidate’s suitability to work with children and young people. The process will include:

  • Meeting with a panel of our pupils for informal question and answer session;

  • Practical Task;

  • Interview with Headteacher, Associate Headteacher and/or Senior Leaders.

Early applications are welcome, and we reserve the right to appoint before the closing date if we find a suitable candidate.

Closing Date: Wednesday 4th November 2026

Interview Date: To be confirmed

Equal Opportunities

At Kingston Educational Trust, we believe that diversity enriches our school community and enhances the educational experience for all. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment that respects and celebrates the unique backgrounds, perspectives, and talents of our staff and students. We welcome applicants from all walks of life and are dedicated to providing equal opportunities for everyone. Join us in fostering a culture of diversity and inclusion where every individual is valued and empowered to thrive.

Safeguarding and Safer Recruitment Statement

The Kingston Academy is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people. We expect all staff and volunteers to share this commitment and undergo appropriate checks, including enhanced DBS checks (with a barred list check for regulated activity), checks with past employers and eligibility to work in the UK. Identity and qualification documents will be checked prior to any offer being made.

We look forward to receiving your application.
